citations.narrative:
The acquisition and disposition records available for review were again not current or complete. The acquisition of
animals obtained (cows, peacocks, pigs) and those disposed of (peacocks, cows, zebu, a rhea, and a budgie) are either
missing all or part of the following: dates of acquisition or disposition, names and addresses of whom the animals were
acquired from or transferred to, their USDA license number and/or Driver’s license number with state of issuance. Other
animals (goats, cows, a nilgai, and zebu) were born on property but not properly documented with full dates of birth.
Without records which fully disclose the animal’s acquisition as well as disposition information, legal and medical
information traceback is not possible. The facility shall ensure that it makes, keeps, and maintains records which fully and
correctly disclose the following information concerning all exhibition animals: the date of the acquisition or disposition, the
species and quantity of animals involved, the name, address, and USDA number, if applicable, of the person from whom
the animal was acquired from or given to, or the vehicle license number and state, as well as the driver’s license number
and state of the person, if not licensed or registered with the Animal Welfare Act. The records shall include any offspring
born of any animal while in his or her possession or under his or her control.

A readily identifiable employee was not present at all times during periods of contact with members of the public. A family
of two adults and one child were observed feeding and touching llamas and emus at the petting zoo area without an
attendant present. Lack of employee oversight of direct interactions between the animals and the visitors may lead to
injury to the public and/or injury or distress to the animals. A responsible, knowledgeable, and readily identifiable
employee or attendant must be present at all times during periods of public contact.
Correct by: 07/01/2026.

citations.desc: Environment enhancement to promote psychological well-being.
citations.narrative:
At the time of inspection, the facility did not provide an adequately detailed species-specific environmental enhancement
plan for all the birds on hand. The facility still has ostriches, emus, and peacocks that were not included in the provided
enrichment plan. A written plan addressing the specific needs of the varied species is necessary to ensure that the overall
health, well-being, and psychological needs of the birds are being appropriately met. The facility must develop, document,
and follow a species-appropriate plan for environment enhancement adequate to promote the psychological well-being of
the birds. The plan must be approved by the attending veterinarian and must address social grouping, environmental
enrichment, special considerations, restraint devices, and exemptions.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The parakeet primary enclosure aviary needed cleaning to remove excess accumulations of excreta. Excreta and food
waste had accumulated along the horizontal wood beams that provided part of the frame of the wire enclosure, closest to
the barn walkway. Also, a free standing wire cage, left open for free access for all the birds as an enrichment item, was
present with excrement covering most surfaces, including not only the wire of the enclosure, but also all perches and
hanging toys hanging within. Regular cleaning is necessary to prevent soiling of the birds and to reduce disease hazards,
insects, pests, and odors. Excreta, debris, and food waste shall be removed from primary enclosures and from under and
around primary enclosures as often as necessary to prevent excessive accumulations.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
